high.title: Oil Price Today (June 29): Crude Oil Rises After Renewed US-Iran Strikes. What Lies Ahead?
high.summary: Crude oil prices are rising sharply following renewed US military strikes on Iranian missile/drone storage facilities and coastal radar sites, after Iran allegedly violated a ceasefire agreement. President Trump's escalatory rhetoric — warning Iran would "no longer exist" if the US resumed full-scale conflict — has injected significant geopolitical risk premium into energy markets.

high.title: Why this matters for INR and Indian markets:

medium.title: Gold, Silver Face Fresh Test as US Dollar, Iran Crisis to Shape Week Ahead: Analysts
medium.summary: Gold and silver are under downward pressure amid escalating US-Iran geopolitical tensions, a strengthening US dollar, and subdued industrial demand weighing on silver. Analysts flag that upcoming macro data — including global manufacturing PMIs, inflation prints, and the US non-farm payrolls report — will be critical in shaping Federal Reserve rate expectations and, by extension, the dollar's trajectory. For INR traders, this combination is worth monitoring closely: a stronger USD environment typically exerts depreciation pressure on the Rupee, while rising crude oil prices stemming from Gulf tensions would widen India's trade deficit and current account gap, adding further headwinds to INR. Gold's direction also matters given India's significant gold import bill — any sustained rally in bullion prices would increase import costs and weigh on the CAD. Watch the US jobs data and Fed commentary carefully this week as key drivers for the DXY and, consequently, USD/INR direction.

medium.title: Ahead of Market: 10 Things That Will Decide Stock Market Action on Tuesday
medium.summary: Indian equities snapped a two-day rally on Monday, with the Sensex declining 372 points and the Nifty 50 shedding 110 points, as escalating Iran-US tensions and profit-booking dampened sentiment. Analysts are recommending a buy-on-dips strategy, citing 23,800 as a key support level for the Nifty. For equity-focused fund managers, the Gulf conflict remains the dominant near-term risk — elevated crude oil prices could pressure India's fiscal position and corporate margins, particularly for energy-intensive sectors. FII flow behaviour will be critical to watch; sustained risk-off sentiment globally could trigger further FPI outflows from Indian equities, which would add depreciation pressure on the INR alongside the crude oil impact.

medium.title: Gold Prices Dip to Rs 1.43 Lakh/10 Grams, Silver Below Rs 2.23 Lakh/Kg. What Lies Ahead?
medium.summary:
Gold and silver futures on MCX declined modestly — gold down ~0.4% and silver down ~0.3% — as renewed Middle East tensions were offset by expectations of further US Federal Reserve rate hikes, which strengthened the USD and pressured non-yielding metals. For INR traders, softer gold prices marginally reduce India's precious metals import bill, offering a slight relief on the trade deficit front. However, the dominant driver here remains the Fed rate hike narrative, which could keep the USD bid and sustain INR depreciation pressure. Watch gold's trajectory as a secondary indicator of global risk sentiment and USD strength.
